title: Man. Post. Cap. II §XIV: Garissoles — primi peccati naming removes homonymy
pass_a_gloss: GAR. But if there were any homonymy and ambiguity in the word of Adam's sin, that nevertheless is wholly removed when the imputation of the first sin of Adam is named. For so each one by himself can easily understand, since there were many sins of Adam, that inquiry is made concerning that one which among all was first, and than which nothing else is prior in the human race. For where there is dealing about number or order, all understand that that is said first from which the principle of number and of order is drawn, and than which nothing is prior in that order. Therefore the Reader was not here to be distinguished by those subtleties of distinctions, that is, more to be disturbed than instructed.
pass_b_english: Garissoles: But if there were any homonymy or ambiguity in the word "Adam's sin," it is wholly removed once we name the imputation of Adam's first sin. Anyone can see for himself that, though Adam had many sins, the question concerns the one that was first among them—nothing earlier in the human race. Where number or order is in view, everyone understands by "first" that from which the series begins, and before which nothing stands in that order. So the reader did not need to be tangled in these subtleties of distinction—that is, more disturbed than taught.
source_text: GAR. Quod si aliqua esset in voce peccati Adae, homonymia & ambiguitas, illa tamen omnino sublata est, cum imputatio primi peccati Adae nuncupatur. Ita enim unusquisque per se facile intelligere potest, cum plura fuerint Adami peccata, de uno illo quaeri, quod inter omnia primum fuit, & quo non aliud est in genere humano prius. Ubi enim de numero vel ordine agitur, primum illud dici omnes intelligunt, unde ducitur numeri ordinisque principium, & quo prius nihil est in illo ordine. Itaque non erat hic istis distinctionum argutiis distinguendus, id est obturbandus magis, quam instruendus Lector.

choices.choice: Primus peccatum naming clears homonymy; stop argutiae
